exposure: Severity of maternal cardiac disease (mWHO class I-II/III vs. mWHO class III-IV)
outcome: Breastfeeding rate at discharge from delivery-associated hospitalization
cohort: The study included 147 patients managed by a comprehensive cardio-obstetrics program at the University of Alabama at Birmingham, who had at least one prenatal visit with the Cardio-Obstetrics team and delivered at UAB.
finding: There were no significant differences in breastfeeding intent or rates at discharge and postpartum visit between patients with less severe versus more severe maternal cardiac disease, though overall breastfeeding rates dropped significantly by the postpartum visit.
gest_age: Babies of varying gestational ages were included, with mean gestational ages of 36.4 weeks for those born to mothers with more severe cardiac disease and 37.7 weeks for those born to mothers with less severe disease.
